research_question: For the first uncovered quartic lift m=8, can a nondegenerate phase A(x^8+b), with A(y)=y^4+beta*y^2+gamma*y and gamma nonzero, lose any one of the four candidate inverse-support classes while retaining the other three?

method.condition_rule: collect every nonzero inverse coefficient whose residue class is outside the three allowed classes
method.elimination: exact Groebner basis over Q in beta,gamma,b,w with grevlex and equation w*gamma-1
method.primary_endpoint: whether the gamma-saturated ideal is the unit ideal for each killed class
secondary_endpoints: Groebner basis and Krull dimension if a saturated locus survives

prospective_predictions.primary: All three gamma-saturated ideals are the unit ideal; no nondegenerate three-class locus survives.
prospective_predictions.secondary: Six distinct confinement conditions are expected for each killed class, matching m=4 through m=7.

adjudication.confirmed: all three saturated ideals are unit ideals
adjudication.falsified: at least one killed class has a nonempty gamma-saturated locus
adjudication.mixed: the primary prediction holds but a secondary prediction fails, or different killed classes have different outcomes
adjudication.inconclusive: the exact computation fails, times out, exhausts resources, or cannot verify the sealed code/protocol hashes

stopping_rule: Run the sealed runner once on all three killed classes. Do not alter depths, equations, monomial order or saturation after inspecting results. Any follow-up is a separately registered successor experiment.
claim_boundary: This is one finite family-blind elimination within the quartic-lift ansatz.
A confirmed result extends the exact quartic-lift computation to m=8 only.
It does not prove the all-degree atlas, the cubic descent, or completeness across all degree-32 polynomials.
A nonempty locus is a candidate requiring exact family interpretation and rank confirmation; it is not automatically a counterexample to every atlas statement.
